title: Atlas onboarding portal hero canvas & step orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Redesign the quickstart landing hero into an adaptable 'portal' canvas that presents the starter steps as an orchestration (instead of static cards). Deliverable assets: hero illustrations (SVG/PNG) with 3 density variants, one-page explainer diagram (desktop/mobile), 6 annotated product screenshots cropped for marketing and docs, and an exportable component library for engineering (tokens, spacing, CTA variants). Goal: reduce cognitive overhead for first-time users, improve conversion to self-serve sign-up, and provide engineers with export-ready assets for the console and docs site.
acceptance_criteria: Hero comp ships with desktop and mobile breakpoints and passes a11y contrast checks
Diagram file includes two levels of information: simple one-line step names and an expanded path with tooltips for each step
All six screenshots exported at 2x and 3x with labelled crop rectangles and alt text in export sheet
Figma file includes component variants (CTA primary/secondary, progress states, microcopy variants) and tokens exported to the design system
Design handoff checklist completed and linked PR created in GitHub with exported assets
tasks: Draft initial hero canvas directions (3 concepts)
Run lightweight usability test with 5 new users for concept preference
Iterate chosen concept into responsive artboards (desktop/tablet/phone)
Produce annotated diagram (simplified + expanded) and callouts for copy team
Capture product screenshots from staging with finalized UI, annotate and export
Prepare Figma handoff with tokens and spec sheet; post assets to Drive and link in PR
comments_updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff — scoped 3 hero concepts. Liam to run engineering feasibility check on in-hero interactive state.
2025-02-24: Usability test (5 participants) completed. Summary: participants preferred a single-column scroll on mobile and a left-anchored diagram on desktop. See research doc link.
2025-02-27: PM review — asked to reduce microcopy length on step 2 and align CTA treatment with console primary button. Action: reduce copy to 6 words maximum; create CTA token mapping.

2025-03-01: Engineering review — noted potential performance issue with animated gradients; agreed to create a static fallback PNG and a lightweight CSS gradient for hosted console. ENG-11234 added to dependencies.
2025-03-03: Design review — design directors approved concept B with minor spacing adjustments. Preparing export-ready files and annotations for handoff.
decisions: Selected concept B (portal canvas with progressive reveal) based on user testing and PM feedback
Use SVG for hero illustrations with PNG fallbacks for older browsers and staging export
Limit hero animation to opacity/translate to avoid GPU-heavy effects; engineering will implement prefers-reduced-motion rules
risks: If staging UI differs from final console release, some screenshots will need re-capture; mitigated by tagging assets with build SHA
Animated hero may impact initial load on low-tier Dedicated instances; fallback PNG required
Copy reductions could affect clarity — plan to A/B short vs. long microcopy in next cycle
handoff_notes: Handoff package includes Figma + export sheet + annotated screenshot directory. Engineering tasks: add prefers-reduced-motion CSS class, implement SVG fallback strategy, confirm responsive image srcset. See handoff checklist in Figma file.
follow_up: Track conversion metrics for the quickstart CTA in console-2025.04 release dashboard
Schedule post-launch 1-week smoke usability check and capture any mismatch between docs screenshots and live UI
